headline: Federal Regulators Unveil Armed Zeppelin Oil Convoys as Revolutionary Gulf Security Strategy
deck: Helium allotments now include munitions; unburned oil ignites new wave of coastal safety measures.
article:
Federal Bureau of Transoceanic Logistics officials rolled out rules allowing armed zeppelin oil convoys at the High-Altitude Bureaucratic Center in Houston. The demo flight featured airships whose helium tanks now double as artillery mounts.

Chief Helio-Logistics Officer Mac D. Windsock called it a direct way to defend fuel routes while adding mid-air target practice. Turnaround times dropped from 19 days to 14 once rooftop cannons became mandatory at every coastal terminal.

The Helium Allotment Board issued dual-use permits covering both heating and weaponry. Coastal homeowners received wind-pattern studies as official reassurance against 300-foot flaming debris zones during gusty skirmishes.

Regulators framed the convoys as routine daily transport, noting that anyone preferring the old system can still book the five-day rail crossing.
author: Clara Windwhistle, Senior Transportation Correspondent

oped.title: Armed Zeppelins: Finally, Someone’s Thinking About My Helium Portfolio
oped.author: Lord Percival F. Gasbag, Esq., Honorary Director of the National Society for Inflated National Security
oped.body: Regulators have finally placed helium where it belongs: inside gun barrels rather than birthday balloons. Complaints about stray shells and burning slicks come only from people who insist on wearing straw hats that soak up oil. My coastal estate has endured enough seepage; I expect the government to issue military-grade pith helmets to every beachgoer at public expense. The true outrage remains the continued rationing of helium for children’s parties while convoys sit idle. The fix is obvious: triple the munitions allocation and send the bill to taxpayers. Rail passengers enduring the five-day crossing will appreciate faster oil delivery overhead, and my mining shares may finally rebound. Progress always requires sacrifice, preferably from someone else.

classifieds.text: FOR SALE: Three surplus helium cylinders, never used for munitions. Seller converting zeppelin to rail freight after federal convoy rules took effect; serious offers only, five-day pickup by appointment.

HELP WANTED: Zep crew needed for armed Gulf oil runs. Must accept helium allotments with live munitions; rail passes provided for weekly returns home. Experience with unburned oil fires preferred, desperation accepted.

LOST & FOUND: Misplaced coastal property deed during last zeppelin convoy ignition event. Finder may keep the ash; owner seeking new liner passage out of the Gulf before regulators expand the program.

PUBLIC NOTICE: The undersigned zeppelin line apologizes for any coastal fires caused by our oil shipments. Effective immediately we are switching to unarmed rail, pending helium reallocation hearings next month.

sponsor_ads.body: Upgrade your personal zeppelin with valves rated for federal convoy speeds; federal regulators confirm they survive 20mm flak at 300 feet. Now boarding with your next oil manifest.

sponsor_ads.headline: Five-Day Rail: The Only Way East Without a Gunner
sponsor_ads.body: Cross the continent in the time it takes an armed zeppelin convoy to refuel twice. No radar signatures, no mid-air boarding parties, just scenery and whatever the dining car still calls coffee.
sponsor_ads.tagline: Complimentary earplugs for when the Gulf zeppelins pass overhead.

sponsor_ads.headline: Gulf Oil: Now With Federal Flak Coverage
sponsor_ads.body: Every barrel delivered under armed zeppelin escort arrives pre-stamped with the new regulatory seal. Tastes the same, costs more, and your shareholders finally stop asking about piracy deductibles.
sponsor_ads.tagline: Batteries not included; neither are lifeboats.

sponsor_ads.headline: Zeppelin Widow Insurance, Gulf Division
sponsor_ads.body: One premium covers both the standard maritime loss and the new federal convoy clause. Payouts double if your spouse’s airship is downed by anything the regulators later classify as ‘revolutionary.’

stories.headline: Gulf Refiners Shift to Night Zeppelin Slots After Helium Allotment Cuts
stories.deck: Petroleum Association warns that munitions priority could delay 14 percent of scheduled crude deliveries this quarter.
stories.article:
Texas coast refiners are now bidding for overnight berths at Houston and New Orleans so their zeppelins can claim the first helium draws. Several companies have shifted cargo to rail tankers to fill the four-day gaps left by convoy delays.

The Petroleum Logistics Board added nine-hour safety inspections at every docking tower after unburned crude residue from test flights kept igniting on contact.

stories.headline: Rail Freight Thefts Rise as Security Focus Moves to Gulf Zeppelins
stories.deck: FBI logs show a 27 percent increase in sealed-car break-ins between Chicago and Denver since convoy patrols began.
stories.article:
Rail police report thieves exploiting the thinned patrols on transcontinental lines while federal agents guard armed helium convoys. Stolen items now include industrial solvents once reserved for zeppelin upkeep.

Agents in Des Moines recovered six empty tanker cars at a siding untouched by federal inspection since March.
